remaining_concerns: The exposed cybersecurity alert triage segment remains below target and is still eligible for the initial rollout.
The policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The rollout controls do not exclude the affected use case, so they do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the cybersecurity alert triage exposure.
The certification position is still not backed by admissible evidence that the policy threshold was met before launch.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position by reinterpreting the existing record. That narrower framing is directionally more accurate, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the unresolved issue is not merely disclosure style or documentation quality; it is an unmet compliance predicate in the available record. The evidence still shows: the cybersecurity alert triage use case remains below target and exposed in the 9% rollout cohort; rollout controls are random by tenant and do not exclude the affected segment; the only risk acceptance is an unapproved draft that does not address this exposure; and the governing policy says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed unless there is approved risk acceptance. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, rollback capability, and monitoring are relevant supporting controls, but they do not satisfy the stated launch condition. Because no genuinely new admissible evidence closed any of the initial concerns, the final assessment remains noncompliant.
